name: list_my_events
title: List my events
description: The upcoming Grateful Giraffes events this person hosts, and the landing pages they can edit ("a page, not an event"), with their page links and whether the page's words can be edited here.

name: get_page
title: Read an event page
description: Everything on an event page that can be changed: each section's words (current and original), photos, the sections the hosts added, the event name and place line, and the run of show. On a landing page: its words, the sections added to it, and where a new section shows (places). Read this before changing anything. eyebrow = the small heading above, title = the headline, body = the paragraph, footer = the hosted-by line, where = the place line, line / serif / note = the request card's first line, highlighted line and small print. edition = an italic subtitle under the opening's headline (e.g. the city), close = a closing line under the run of show. A line break (\n) starts a new line on the page.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

name: update_page
title: Change page words
description: Change the words of the page's sections. Only the fields you name change. Set a field to null to go back to its original words; list a section in reset to put the whole section back. eyebrow = the small heading above, title = the headline, body = the paragraph, footer = the hosted-by line, where = the place line, line / serif / note = the request card's first line, highlighted line and small print. edition = an italic subtitle under the opening's headline (e.g. the city), close = a closing line under the run of show. A line break (\n) starts a new line on the page.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

reset.description: Sections to put back to their original words (their photos stay)

name: add_section
title: Add a page section
description: Add a new section to the page: a photo with a heading, headline, paragraph and hosted-by line, placed after a section (or after another added section). Up to 6. On an event page the photo is needed, a direct https link to a JPG or PNG. On a landing page the photo is optional (a JPG, PNG or WebP) and words only is fine; get_page (places) says where it shows. The reply gives the new section's id, for update_section and remove_section.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

after.description: The section (or added section id) it goes after

name: update_section
title: Change an added section
description: Change a section the hosts added: its words, where it goes, or its photo (a direct https link to a JPG or PNG, or a WebP on a landing page). Fields you leave out stay; null clears a field.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

id.description: The added section's id from get_page

name: remove_section
title: Remove an added section
description: Remove a section the hosts added. Anything placed after it moves up.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

name: set_photo
title: Set a section photo
description: Give one of the page's own sections a new photo from a direct https link to a JPG or PNG (cropped and darkened to match the page), or photo_url null to go back to the original photo. section "stage" is the opening animation's first (afternoon) frame. On a landing page, section is the id of a section added to it (a JPG, PNG or WebP; null takes its photo off); the page's own photos stay.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

name: update_style
title: Change the page look
description: Event pages only. Change how the page looks: colours, fonts, cursor, the order of the sections, hiding a section, button labels, where the words sit on a section, and the opening animation's two lines. Only what you send changes; null puts that part back to the original; {"reset": true} puts the whole look back. get_page lists the options and what is set now. Colours are refused when text would be hard to read on the background. The opening stays first and the seat section always stays.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

palette.description: Hex colours: gold (accent: lines, small headings), goldl (headlines), ivory (body text), ink (background). e.g. {"gold":"#e0a050"}

fonts.description: A font pair id from get_page (look.fonts)

order.description: Every section once, the opening (hero) first

hidden.description: Sections to hide (not hero or reserve)

buttons.description: Button labels by "section:position", e.g. {"hero:0":"Save my seat"}; null for one goes back

placement.description: Where a section's words sit, phone (m) and desktop (d) separately: {"gathering":{"m":{"v":"top","h":"center","scale":1.1}}}. v = top|middle|bottom, h = left|center|right, scale 0.8 to 1.3

reset.description: true puts the whole look back to the original

layout.description: Pages made in the Host Studio only: onefold (one screen), poster, letter or classic

palette_name.description: Pages made in the Host Studio only: a named palette, which replaces hand-set colours

name: set_share
title: Make the share preview
description: Event pages only. Make the share preview: the picture and words WhatsApp, iMessage and Slack show when someone shares the event's grateful.gg link. A 1200x630 card with the title and date set large on one of the page's photos. Only what you send changes; get_page (share) shows what's set now and the photos to pick from. preview_only true draws the card and returns its link without saving, so the person can see it first. Saved cards show on grateful.gg in about a minute.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

photo.description: A photo id from get_page share.photos ("hero", "stage" for the opening animation, a section) or a direct https link to a JPG or PNG

focus.description: What to keep in view when cropping to the card, [across, down] from 0 to 1, e.g. [0.75, 0.5] keeps the right side

side.description: Which side the words sit on (put them over the quieter part of the photo)

eyebrow.description: Small heading in capitals, e.g. "Grateful Giraffes"

title.description: The big title (\n for a new line)

edition.description: Italic subtitle under the title, e.g. the city

line.description: Small line in capitals at the bottom, e.g. "Doors 7:00 PM CT · Potluck dinner"

desc.description: The sentence chat apps show under the title (not on the picture)

name: update_event
title: Change event details
description: Events only. Change the event's name, its place line, its price, who needs approval, ticket types, or the run of show; for a new event that isn't published yet, also its date and times. For the run of show, send the whole list from get_page with your changes (keep each item's id; items with public false are the hosts' own notes and stay off the page). Use ticket_types for multiple tiers (different prices/times/descriptions); it replaces the single price field when set. A new price is for new RSVPs; guests who already paid keep what they paid. If the page's words mention the price (e.g. the request card), offer to update them too.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

place.description: The short place line, e.g. "West China Tea House · East Austin"

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Only for a new event that isn't published yet

time.description: Start, e.g. "7:00 PM". Only for a new event that isn't published yet

end_time.description: End, e.g. "9:30 PM". Only for a new event that isn't published yet

ticket_types.description: Multiple ticket tiers with different prices/times. Replaces single price when set. Each tier can be fixed price, free, or sliding scale (pay what feels right). Fixed: {"name":"VIP","priceType":"fixed","price":40}. Free: {"name":"Basic","priceType":"free"}. Sliding: {"name":"General","priceType":"sliding","minPrice":18,"maxPrice":54,"suggestedPrice":36,"priceLabel":"Contribute what feels right"}. Optional: description, time, capacity.

potluck.description: Ask guests what they will bring

gigi_sms.description: Show guests the box for Gigi's SMS updates

waitlist.description: Let people join a waitlist when every seat is taken

capacity.description: How many guests in all; null takes the limit off

approval.description: all_confirm = everyone is in automatically; giraffe_auto = Giraffes are in automatically, everyone else waits for a host; host_all = a host approves every request

name: list_payouts
title: See what the hosts are owed

annotations.title: See what the hosts are owed

description: What the host is owed for their events, as the Payouts page shows it: collected, refunded, Stripe fees, the platform fee, what is owed, what has been paid, what is still outstanding (or due back after a refund following a payout), who the money goes to, and each payout sent. Without event, every event of theirs that has money or payouts; with event, that one. Read only. Bank details are never shown.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

name: move_event
title: Move an event's date
description: Move a live event to a new date (and time), and tell everyone going by email, with an updated calendar invite for those with a seat. Use this, not update_event, once an event is live. Without confirm true it only previews: it returns the old and new date and time, the exact email (subject and text), how many people get it, and a confirm_code, and changes nothing. ALWAYS show the host the email note and the number of guests who will get it, and call again with confirm true and the same confirm_code (and the same settings) ONLY after the host says yes. The code is good for 10 minutes and only for that event, date and time. A move cannot be quietly undone: guests are emailed. subject and message are optional and replace the default note (the cancel line is always added). audience "confirmed" (default) tells guests who are going; "all" also tells those waiting for approval. The page, the calendar invite and the share card follow the new date.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

time.description: New start, e.g. "7:00 PM". Leave out to keep the current one

end_time.description: New end, e.g. "9:30 PM". Leave out to keep the current one

subject.description: Subject of the email to guests. Leave out for the default

message.description: The host's words in the email to guests. Leave out for the default

audience.description: Who is told: "confirmed" (default) or "all" (also those waiting)

confirm.description: Must be true to move the event, and only after the host said yes to the preview

confirm_code.description: The confirm_code from the preview, passed back with confirm true

name: make_photo
title: Make a photo
description: Make a new photo for any photo on an event page from a few words, using the hosts' monthly AI photo budget. Three calls: with section (an id from get_page, share.photos, e.g. "stage" for the opening animation) and prompt it starts and returns a job; with job it checks on it, and when ready returns both versions (phone and desktop links); with job and use true it puts the pair on the page. Wait about 20 seconds between checks. ALWAYS show the person both versions and use them only after they say yes. Only the use call changes the page. It is live for everyone at once; the original can be restored in the page editor.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

section.description: Which photo: an id from get_page share.photos

prompt.description: A few words describing the photo, e.g. "a candlelit rooftop at dusk, seen from behind the guests"

job.description: The job from the first call, to check on it or use it

use.description: With job: true puts the finished photo on the page, only after the person said yes

name: create_event
title: Create a draft event
description: Approved hosts only: start a new event page on the Oasis, as a draft at app.grateful.gg/p/<key> with RSVPs closed until publish_event. You write the page's words from what the person tells you, in the Grateful Giraffes voice: warm, poetic, short lines, grounded; never em or en dashes; never invent prices, names, famous guests or promises. The page is a poster in four sections (sections): hero (the opening, over a big photo), gathering (what it is and who it's for), evening (the run of show heading) and reserve (the RSVP card). Give a photo_url (a direct https link to a JPG, PNG or WebP of theirs), or leave it out and add the opening photo later with set_photo (section "hero"). The street address stays private and goes only to confirmed guests. Guests RSVP on the Oasis for free with approvals by Giraffes first; change the price or approvals with update_event.

title.description: The event's name, e.g. "Full Moon Sound Bath"

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Leave out if not decided yet

time_zone.description: IANA zone from the city, e.g. "America/New_York". Leave out for Los Angeles

city.description: The public place line: a city or neighbourhood, never a street address, e.g. "Venice"

venue.description: A venue name if it is a public place

address.description: The street address. Private: only confirmed guests get it

hosts.description: The hosts' names as the page shows them, e.g. "Juliet & Max"

sections.description: The page's words. gathering.title and gathering.body are needed; fill in all four for a full page. \n starts a new line.

eyebrow.description: Tiny line above the title, usually "Grateful Giraffes"

where.description: One short line on what it is, e.g. "An intimate potluck dinner"

eyebrow.description: The date in words, e.g. "Friday, November 14"

close.description: One short line under the schedule, e.g. "Ends about 9:00 PM"

body.description: One or two short lines on what to bring or expect

palette.description: The page's colours, by mood: dusk (warm gold on a deep night blue, candlelit and calm); ember (fire orange on smoky plum, a party, a bonfire, a celebration); ocean (sea glass on deep water, the beach, breath, sound baths); forest (sage and moss on a dark wood, hikes, gardens, retreats); rose (rose on dark wine, love, women's circles, tenderness); violet (lavender on indigo, meditation, music, the cosmos); sand (desert clay on dark earth, ceremony, the land, slow dinners)

photo_url.description: Their own photo for the opening: a direct https link to a JPG, PNG or WebP

ticket_url.description: Only if guests buy tickets somewhere else (Luma, Eventbrite): that link, and the page sends them there instead of RSVPing on the Oasis

name: make_art
title: Make 4 opening images
description: Make four versions of a new event's opening image from a description, each in its own look (cinematic, up close, painted, graphic). It takes about 20 seconds and shows them. Nothing goes on the page until choose_art. Show the person all four, ask which they like, and pass on the link it gives to see them large.

event.description: The event key create_event gave back (or from list_my_events)

description.description: The picture in a sentence or two, in the person's words: the place, the light, the feeling. No words or names to appear in it

name: change_art
title: Change one opening image
description: The person's feedback on one image: makes four new takes of that image with the change. Nothing goes on the page until choose_art.

event.description: The event key create_event gave back (or from list_my_events)

option.description: Which image: 1 to 4 in the newest round, or its id, e.g. "r1-3"

feedback.description: What to change, in the person's words

name: show_art
title: Show the opening images
description: Show the newest four images for a new event again, and which is on the page.

event.description: The event key create_event gave back (or from list_my_events)

name: choose_art
title: Use an opening image
description: Put the image the person chose on the event page as its opening, sized for phones and computers. It takes about 30 seconds. Only after they have said which one.

event.description: The event key create_event gave back (or from list_my_events)

option.description: Which image: 1 to 4 in the newest round, or its id, e.g. "r1-3"

name: publish_event
title: Publish an event
description: Put a new event live: RSVPs open, and its grateful.gg share link (with a preview card made from the page's photo and words) is made. Only after the person has seen the draft page and said yes. It needs its opening photo first.

event.description: The event key create_event gave back (or from list_my_events)

name: upload_event_page
title: Upload a landing page
description: Upload a whole landing page of the host's own design for their event, as a draft. Returns a preview link only the event's hosts can open; nothing changes for guests until publish_event_page. Make one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and JS are fine, fonts and media by https link). Use add_page_asset to keep each picture or video from an AI tool, since their links expire. The Oasis keeps its own RSVP button pinned at the bottom of the screen, so leave room for it there; any element with a data-oasis-rsvp attribute, or a link to #rsvp, also opens the RSVP. Links open in a new tab. Never put a price, a street address or a sign-in form on the page: checkout and the guest emails carry those. Make it work on a phone (390 wide) and a laptop (1280 wide).

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "cosmic-nov-8"

html.description: The whole page: one HTML document, at most 2 MB

note.description: What changed in this version, in a few words

name: get_event_page
title: Read the uploaded page
description: The HTML of the event's uploaded page to revise: the waiting draft if there is one, else the live one. Says so when the event has none.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "cosmic-nov-8"

name: add_page_asset
title: Keep a picture or video for a page

annotations.title: Keep a picture or video for a page

description: Copy a picture (JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to 15 MB) or a video (MP4 or WebM, up to 60 MB) from a direct https link into the Oasis, and get back a link that lasts, to use in an uploaded page.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "cosmic-nov-8"

url.description: A direct https link to the file

name: publish_event_page
title: Publish the uploaded page
description: Make the latest uploaded draft the event's page, for everyone at once. Only after the host has opened the preview link and said yes.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "cosmic-nov-8"

name: remove_event_page
title: Go back to the Oasis page

annotations.title: Go back to the Oasis page

description: Take the uploaded page down and show the event's standard Oasis page again. The uploaded versions are kept.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "cosmic-nov-8"

name: list_guests
title: List guests
description: Who is coming to an event, as the host panel shows it: name, email, phone (if any), status (going, pending, waitlist, declined or removed), party size, whether they are checked in, whether they paid, and the id to use with the other guest tools. Also counts for each status. Without status it lists going, pending and waitlist; use "all" to include declined and removed.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

name: add_guests
title: Add guests
description: Add people straight to Going, up to 100 at a time. Each needs a name and an email; a phone is optional. By default each person gets the confirmation email with the address, so check the list with the host first. send_email false adds them quietly. Anyone already going is skipped. Anyone who already asked to come (pending or waitlist) has to be approved with decide_guest.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

send_email.description: Send each guest the confirmation email (default true)

name: check_in
title: Check a guest in
description: Check a guest in at the door. Without count, the whole party is checked in. count is how many of the party are in (never more than their tickets); count 0 checks them out.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

guest_id.description: The guest's registration id from list_guests

name: remove_guest
title: Remove a guest
description: Take a guest off the list quietly: no email goes to them and their seat is freed. A guest who paid has to be refunded first, then removed. They show as removed in list_guests and can be put back with restore_guest.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

guest_id.description: The guest's registration id from list_guests

name: restore_guest
title: Restore a removed guest
description: Put back a guest a host removed. They return to Going only if they had a confirmed seat before; otherwise they come back as pending and a host approves them with decide_guest. Works only for guests removed by a host.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

guest_id.description: The guest's registration id from list_guests

name: message_guests
title: Email guests
description: Email the guests of an event, signed by the hosts. Always use mode "preview" first: it sends nothing and returns the exact email text and how many people get it. Show the host that message and the number, and send only after the host says yes. mode "test" sends one copy to the host only. mode "send" emails everyone in the audience and also needs confirm true. Keep the message warm and short, with no em dashes. Never send a message the host has not seen.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

audience.description: confirmed = going, pending = waiting for a host, waitlist = waiting for a spot, all = every one of those

message.description: The email, after "Hi [first name],". A blank line starts a new paragraph.

confirm.description: Must be true for mode "send", and only after the host said yes to the preview

name: decide_guest
title: Approve or decline a guest
description: Approve or decline a guest who asked to come (pending or waitlist), the same as the Approve and Decline buttons in the host panel. Approving charges their card hold, if they have one, and emails their confirmation with the address. Declining releases the hold and emails them a kind no. Without confirm true this only previews and returns a confirm_code; show the host what will happen and decide only after they say yes, by calling again with confirm true and the same confirm_code (good for 10 minutes). If the room is full, it says so; ask the host, and only if they say yes call again with over_capacity true. A decision cannot be undone, apart from approving someone a host declined.

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

guest_id.description: The guest's registration id from list_guests

over_capacity.description: Approve even though the room is full, only after the host said yes to that

confirm.description: Must be true to decide, and only after the host said yes to the preview

confirm_code.description: The confirm_code from the preview, passed back with confirm true

name: fill_waitlist
title: Fill open seats from the waitlist

annotations.title: Fill open seats from the waitlist

description: Give the open seats to the people who have waited longest on the waitlist. Nothing fills by itself: this is the hosts' call. Without confirm true it only previews: who would get a seat (longest wait first), who is passed over and why (a party bigger than the seats left, or on a paid event someone who has not paid), how many stay on the waitlist, and a confirm_code. Show the host that. With confirm true and that confirm_code it seats exactly those people: each one's card hold is charged if they have one, and each gets the confirmation email with the address. If the waitlist or the open seats changed since the preview, nothing happens: preview again. An event with no guest limit has no seats to fill (update_event sets capacity).

event.description: The event key from list_my_events, e.g. "illuminate"

confirm.description: Must be true to seat them, and only after the host said yes to the preview

confirm_code.description: The confirm_code from the preview, passed back with confirm true

name: get_design_system
title: Read the Oasis design brief
description: The Oasis design brief: what the Oasis is, its main pages, its look (canvas, type, mood) and the rules every page keeps, plus how to shape a mockup for submit_design_idea. For the Grateful Giraffes team and approved hosts.

name: submit_design_idea
title: Submit a design idea
description: Send the Grateful Giraffes team a design improvement for the Oasis: a title, the page, what is wrong today, what to change and why, and a self-contained HTML mockup (inline CSS, no scripts, under 300 KB). It is saved for review; nothing on the Oasis changes. Show the person the idea before sending.

title.description: The idea in a few words

page_url.description: The Oasis page it improves, e.g. https://app.grateful.gg/events (leave out for the whole Oasis)

problem.description: What is wrong or could be better today

proposal.description: What to change, and why it is better

mockup_html.description: A self-contained HTML mockup: inline CSS, no scripts, phone and laptop versions

name: list_my_design_ideas
title: List my design ideas
description: The design ideas this person sent, newest first, with their status (new, approved, passed or built) and the review note.
